content.title: About
content.content: Mint Julep is a classic Southern United States cocktail made with bourbon, fresh mint, sugar and water. It is known for its refreshing flavor and aroma, usually served in a chilled julep cup with crushed ice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink originated in the early 19th century and became popular in Kentucky, especially in Lexington.
Traditionally it is served in a julep cup, which has a wide base and a narrow rim.
The original recipe uses a simple syrup (sugar + water), but many modern versions replace it with honey or agave.
Mint Julep is closely associated with the Kentucky Derby, where it is considered the official beverage of the event.
Mint leaves are often gently muddled before adding to the cocktail to release more aroma.

items.title: Contains mint
items.content: Mint is rich in menthol, which can aid digestion and provide a mild soothing effect.

items.title: Bourbon in moderation
items.content: Bourbon contains antioxidants such as polyphenols that may support cardiovascular health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: The scent of mint is often used in aromatherapy to reduce anxiety and improve mood.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive alcohol consumption can lead to liver problems, dependence, and other health risks.

items.title: Sugar
items.content: Simple syrup adds calories and can contribute to tooth decay and blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Mint allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to mint, resulting in skin rashes or swelling.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve Mint Julep in a chilled julep cup, gently muddle mint leaves, add bourbon, simple syrup, and top with cold water. Fill with crushed ice and garnish with a sprig of mint.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store alcoholic beverages in a cool, dark place. Keep simple syrup refrigerated in a sealed bottle for up to a month. Fresh mint should be stored in the refrigerator wrapped in a damp paper towel and used within a few days.
